skill.name: council
skill.description: Run a model-diverse subagent council to investigate the same problem from multiple perspectives, compare findings, and produce a final recommendation. Use this skill whenever the user asks for a council, second opinions, multiple agents/models to evaluate one question, parallel investigation, red-team/blue-team comparison, or help deciding between competing technical approaches.
skill.summary: Coordinate diverse subagents, compare evidence, and deliver one clear recommendation.
skill.author: warpdotdev

content.user_title: Compare Decisions with an AI Council
content.value_statement: Complex decisions can suffer from narrow analysis and hidden assumptions. This skill coordinates diverse agents, compares their evidence, and produces one actionable recommendation.
actual_capabilities: Frames one decision question with explicit options, evidence sources, constraints, and success criteria.
Assigns different models and analytical perspectives to reduce redundant council reports.
Coordinates read-only investigations or isolated implementation work across multiple subagents.
Requests structured reports covering evidence, risks, costs, recommendations, confidence, and unknowns.
Synthesizes consensus and disagreements into a concise decision memo with concrete next steps.
limitations: Requires an environment that can launch and communicate with multiple subagents.
Available model diversity depends on the active harness and configured providers.
Recommendations remain limited by the evidence and repository context supplied to each agent.
The skill does not independently verify every claim beyond comparing cited evidence.

use_cases.title: Review an architecture choice
use_cases.description: Compare competing designs for correctness, implementation cost, operational risk, and testability before committing to one approach.

use_cases.title: Challenge a risky code change
use_cases.description: Ask independent reviewers to inspect a proposed fix for regressions, security concerns, and missing tests.

use_cases.title: Assess an incident response
use_cases.description: Combine implementation, reliability, and contrarian perspectives into a prioritized recovery and prevention recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Get a second opinion
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a council on [question]. Compare [option A] and [option B], then recommend one using [decision criteria].
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs independent perspectives on a clear choice.

prompt_templates.title: Review a technical proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Form a read-only council to review [proposal or artifact]. Assess correctness, implementation effort, testing needs, and operational risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team wants structured feedback before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Red-team a planned change
prompt_templates.prompt: Use diverse models to evaluate [change]. Assign architecture, implementation, and adversarial perspectives. Cite evidence and identify unresolved assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineering lead wants deeper scrutiny of a risky change.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an evidence-weighted decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate [decision] with a model-diverse council. Compare findings by evidence quality, resolve disagreements, and separate immediate actions from optional hardening.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a decision memo for a complex tradeoff.

output_examples.input: Should we keep the current cache or adopt the proposed distributed cache?
output_examples.output: Recommendation: keep the current cache for this release. The proposal improves scale, but migration risk and weak failure testing outweigh the immediate benefit.

output_examples.input: Review this authentication fix from correctness, security, and rollout perspectives.
output: Consensus: the fix closes the reported bypass.
Disagreement: reviewers differ on session invalidation scope.
Next step: add expiration tests and deploy behind staged monitoring.

output_examples.input: Decide whether to refactor now or stabilize the current implementation.
output_examples.output: Final call: stabilize first, measure the remaining defects, and schedule the refactor only if the measured maintenance cost justifies it.

best_practices: Define one precise decision, relevant artifacts, constraints, and evaluation criteria before launching the council.
Use distinct models and perspectives, then judge reports by cited evidence instead of vote count.
Keep read-only agents from editing files and isolate implementation agents in separate worktrees.
anti_patterns: Do not launch several agents with identical models, prompts, and analytical roles.
Do not treat lifecycle completion as proof that a report contains useful evidence.
Do not present raw agent transcripts when the user needs a concise recommendation.

faq.question: What problems suit this skill?
faq.answer: It works best for architecture choices, risky fixes, code reviews, rollout decisions, incident analysis, and other judgment-heavy questions.

faq.question: Does every council require three agents?
faq.answer: No. Three diverse members are the preferred default, but availability, scope, and user constraints can justify another size.

faq.question: Can council members edit code?
faq.answer: Yes, when requested. Each local implementation agent should use an isolated worktree and branch to prevent conflicts.

faq.question: What happens when model diversity is unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill uses the closest supported models and preserves diversity through distinct specialist or adversarial perspectives.

faq.question: How are conflicting recommendations resolved?
faq.answer: The final synthesis weighs evidence quality, decision criteria, risks, and unknowns instead of choosing the majority view.

faq.question: Does the skill guarantee a correct decision?
faq.answer: No. Its recommendation depends on available evidence, agent capabilities, and the accuracy of the supplied context.
